# django-mojo: dnsman — unified domain / DNS / email / SSL management

- **Kind**: feature
- **Date**: 2026-07-25
- **Requested by**: Ian (ian@nativemojo.com)
- **Repo**: django-mojo (`/Users/ians/Projects/mojo/nativemojo/django-mojo`) — framework work, built in a django-mojo session per the working agreement
- **Relation**: maestro item **#391** (Sites & Domains epic) is PARKED pending this — its Phase 1 re-scopes to consume dnsman instead of building an in-app route53 service
- **Build routing**: inline, session

## Description

A new framework app that makes domain-name management KISS — one place for domains, host entries, email setup, and SSL, replacing today's scattered pieces. Core API features (requester's list):

1. **Search for available domains** (with live pricing).
2. **Purchase a domain** via AWS Route53 Domains — optionally associated with an `account.Group`, tracking **our core cost** and **purchase history** (which user and/or group made the purchase). Maestro extends this for user-based purchases; dnsman itself carries no end-user purchase policy.
3. **Manage WHOIS/ICANN information**, including private registration. (Answered at intake: **AWS supports it** — `PrivacyProtect{Admin,Registrant,Tech}Contact` flags on register + `update_domain_contact_privacy`, free, WHOIS shows the registrar proxy instead of the real contact. Not available on a few TLDs (e.g. `.us` forbids privacy) — expose a per-TLD capability flag. Default privacy ON.)
4. **Manage DNS host entries** — record CRUD, provider-dispatched (see 5).
5. **Existing GoDaddy-hosted domains supported OUT OF THE GATE** (requester direction 2026-07-25): link a GoDaddy API key/account to our system; a Domain marked `provider="godaddy"` routes all DNS management through the linked credential instead of Route53. Credentials are **forced** for GoDaddy-backed domains — no linked working credential, no DNS operations (fail closed).
6. **Easy email setup** — even easier with this flow, and for BOTH providers: `ses_domain.py` computes the records; `apply_dns_records_godaddy` already exists, the route53 twin gets built here, and the provider dispatch picks the right one — `EmailDomain` onboarding approaches one call either way. Includes an **audit of the current email setup** (email_ops, `aws/setup_dns.py`, `EmailDomain`) — and fix the known `EmailDomain` default-graph leak (`aws_key` returned unmasked; logged in maestro's `docs/AttentionNeeded.md`).
7. **SSL certificate management with central custody** (see Decisions — resolves the "republish to a new EC2" problem). Central DNS-01 issuance works across BOTH providers, because it only needs a TXT record planted wherever the zone lives.

## Context

The framework already holds the pieces, separately and unevenly: GoDaddy `DNSManager` (`mojo/helpers/dns/godaddy.py` — records only), read-only inspection (`mojo/helpers/domain.py`), SES onboarding (`mojo/helpers/aws/ses_domain.py` + `EmailDomain` with a `dns_mode="route53"` stub that has never been implemented), no Route53 helper, no cert management at all. Maestro's #391 scoped a sites/domains product and initially planned the registrar service in-app with "graduate later"; the split decision (project 9 KB, kind=decision, "Sites & Domains — django-mojo vs maestro split") says **mechanism → framework, policy → maestro** — and the requester has called framework-first: dnsman IS the mechanism layer, other NativeMojo products get it for free, and maestro's sites app slims to policy (user purchases, credits/gates, MCP, portal, hosting). The `EmailDomain.dns_mode` choice field is the in-repo precedent for per-domain provider dispatch — dnsman generalizes it.

## Decisions (from intake discussion, 2026-07-25)

- **Registrar = AWS Route53 Domains.** Research on #391's trail: GoDaddy purchase API is gated (50+ domains, prepaid Good-as-Gold, 20k calls/month); `route53domains` has no gates, `register_domain` auto-creates the hosted zone + auto-renews, and the client is **us-east-1 only**. **Purchase is Route53-only**; GoDaddy-backed domains are management-only, and purchase attempts on them refuse with a clear error.
- **Provider dispatch + linked credentials (BYO GoDaddy)**: `Domain.provider` ∈ `route53 | godaddy`. Credentials live in a dedicated **`DnsCredential`** model (`MojoSecrets` key/secret, optional `group` FK for tenant ownership, masked graphs, rotation support) — NOT on the Domain row, because one GoDaddy account holds many domains and rotation must happen in one place. Domain FKs its credential. **The working credential IS the proof of control** for self-serve BYO onboarding: at link/registration time we verify via the GoDaddy API that the account actually holds the domain (`get_domain_info`/`is_domain_active` probe, stored `verified` flag + last error) — no manual adoption step needed. Blast-radius caution: a GoDaddy key is account-wide, so only domains explicitly registered AND verified in our system are manageable through it; no "list everything in the account" surface for general members.
- **Private registration: yes, default ON**, per-TLD capability surfaced.
- **SSL: dnsman owns cert custody AND issuance, centrally.** A `Certificate` model holding cert/chain PEM and the private key **KMS-envelope-encrypted via `KSMSecrets`** (`mojo/models/secrets.py` — exists for exactly this "protected cloud" need), issued via **ACME DNS-01** — a pure API operation needing no webserver, so issuance and renewal run centrally (worker/cron), not on serving boxes. **DNS-01 rides the provider dispatch**: TXT `_acme-challenge` planted via Route53 *or* the linked GoDaddy credential (`DNSManager.add_record` handles TXT), so BYO-GoDaddy domains get the same central certs. GoDaddy caveat: no ChangeInfo-style propagation API, so the issuance flow polls public DNS for the TXT before asking the CA to validate. Serving hosts (maestro's sites EC2, any product box) are dumb consumers that **sync cert material down via a job channel** and reload locally. Republishing to a new EC2 = bootstrap + sync job: **zero re-issuance, no Let's Encrypt rate-limit exposure, boxes become cattle**. HTTP-01-on-box remains a documented later fallback for domains whose DNS we can't touch at all. Deployment/reload mechanics stay product-side.
- **Purchase-history attribution lives in dnsman** (generic: user, optional group, our cost, operation trail); end-user-facing purchase POLICY (quote/confirm UX, allowlists, spend caps, credits) stays in maestro.

- [ ] `mojo/helpers/aws/route53.py` — Domains + hosted-zone/record primitives (availability incl. tri-state `PENDING`/`DONT_KNOW` + `INVALID_NAME_FOR_TLD`, register, operation polling, prices, zones, record CRUD with NS/SOA + in-zone guards, pagination; us-east-1 client for Domains)
- [ ] `mojo/apps/dnsman/` app (one model per file, mojo conventions): `Domain` (optional `group` FK, `provider`, credential FK, status lifecycle, zone id, auto_renew/privacy, expiry), `DnsCredential` (`MojoSecrets`; group-owned; verified flag; rotation), `DomainPurchase` (user + group + our cost + operation id + status — the purchase-history ledger), `Certificate` (`KSMSecrets`; keys never in any graph)
- [ ] **Provider dispatch**: one service surface for record CRUD/apply that routes by `Domain.provider`; GoDaddy-backed domains achieve record-management parity (purchase/zone-create refuse with a clear "management-only" error); missing/broken credential → fail-closed with an actionable error
- [ ] BYO onboarding: link a GoDaddy credential, register an existing domain against it, ownership verified via API probe — self-serve, no operator step
- [ ] Purchase flow with the #391-hardened money semantics ported in: compare-and-swap under `select_for_update`, durable-intent-before-AWS-call ordering, no-failed-rows invariant, `list_operations` reconciliation for the crash window, ICANN registrant-email-verification + 60-day-lock documented in the runbook
- [ ] WHOIS contact get/update + privacy toggle endpoints
- [ ] Email: provider-dispatched record apply (`apply_dns_records_godaddy` exists; build the route53 twin) + one-call `EmailDomain` onboarding for dnsman-held domains; email-setup audit written up; `EmailDomain` `aws_key` graph leak fixed
- [ ] Certificates: DNS-01 issue + renewal cron working over BOTH providers (with the GoDaddy propagation-poll step) + a sync/export surface consumers can pull from a job channel; renewal state visible
- [ ] Fail-closed permissions on every endpoint (a `manage_dns`-style vocabulary; group-scoped where a row has a group); zero secrets in graphs
- [ ] Tests with boto + GoDaddy HTTP fully mocked (no live AWS/GoDaddy anywhere); docs in both dm tracks; CHANGELOG

- `mojo/helpers/dns/godaddy.py` — 62 lines: `DNSManager(api_key, api_secret)` with `get_domains`, `get_domain_info`, `is_domain_active`, `get_record`/`get_records`, `add_record`/`edit_record`/`bulk_add_records` — everything BYO management + ACME TXT planting needs; no purchase calls. GoDaddy's DNS-tier API needs only 1+ domain in the caller's account (the user's own account qualifies by definition).
- `mojo/helpers/domain.py` — `is_available`/`whois`/`ssl` inspection. `mojo/helpers/aws/ses_domain.py` (1105 lines) — `onboard_domain`, `build_required_dns_records`, `apply_dns_records_godaddy` (line ~1074); the route53 twin is the missing piece. `EmailDomain(MojoSecrets, MojoModel)` — `dns_mode` manual|route53|godaddy, route53 unimplemented.
- `mojo/helpers/aws/` has `client.py`/`ec2.py`/`s3.py`/`ses*.py` — no `route53.py`/`acm.py`. `KSMSecrets` (KMS envelope) in `mojo/models/secrets.py`.
- boto3 `route53domains` verified offline in the maestro venv (2026-07-25): `check_domain_availability`, `register_domain`, `list_prices`, `get_operation_detail`, `list_operations`, `enable/disable_domain_auto_renew`, `update_domain_contact_privacy` all present; availability enum includes `PENDING`/`DONT_KNOW`/`INVALID_NAME_FOR_TLD`/`UNAVAILABLE_PREMIUM`.
- Jobs channels are the consumer-sync mechanism: `jobs.publish(channel=…)`, channel-scoped runners (`mojo/apps/jobs/manager.py`, `JOBS_CHANNELS`).
- Cert economics (verified 2026-07-25): free ACM certs attach only to ALB/CloudFront; exportable ACM is $7/FQDN + $79/wildcard per issuance AND renewal on 198-day validity — Let's Encrypt via ACME is $0 and DNS-01 works centrally because we control (or hold credentials for) the zones.

- End-user purchase policy, credits, allowlists, quote/confirm UX (maestro sites app — #391).

## Plan

**Scoped 2026-07-25, in the django-mojo repo with full code access.** Requester decisions taken during scoping:

- **One plan, one build** — no phase split, no sub-items. The whole of dnsman lands in a single `/maestro-build 392` session. The implementation below is ordered into seven stages with explicit commit boundaries so a session that has to stop still leaves the tree coherent and green.
- **First-value ordering**: foundation + purchase come first (stages 1–4), then email (stage 5), then certificates (stage 6). This is the order that unparks #391 fastest.
- **ACME client: written in-repo** (requester deferred to recommendation). Rationale under Design decisions §7.

### Objective

A new framework app `mojo/apps/dnsman/` plus a `mojo/helpers/aws/route53.py` primitive layer that together make one API surface for: searching + buying domains through Route53 Domains, managing DNS records on either Route53 or a BYO GoDaddy account behind one dispatch, reading/updating WHOIS contacts and privacy, applying SES email records through that same dispatch, and centrally issuing/renewing/custodying Let's Encrypt certificates via ACME DNS-01 with KMS-encrypted private keys and a job-channel sync surface for serving boxes. Mechanism only — no end-user purchase policy, no hosting, no cert installation.

### Architecture (locked)

**App**: `mojo/apps/dnsman/` — standard mojo app layout (`apps.py`, `models/` one per file, `rest/`, `services/`, `services/providers/`, `migrations/`, `cronjobs.py`, `asyncjobs.py`). Registered by adding `"mojo.apps.dnsman"` to the INSTALLED_APPS list in `bin/create_testproject` (line ~111 block, after `mojo.apps.aws`). URL prefix is the app directory name → `/api/dnsman/…` (`mojo/urls.py` derives it from the app label; no extra wiring).

**Provider dispatch**: `Domain.provider ∈ {route53, godaddy}`. One service surface (`services/dns.py`) resolves a `Domain` to a provider adapter and calls a uniform interface. Adapters live in `services/providers/`:

```
list_records(domain)                       -> [objict(type, name, values, ttl)]   # name is FQDN, no trailing dot
upsert_record(domain, rtype, name, values, ttl)
delete_record(domain, rtype, name, values=None)
wait_for_propagation(domain, rtype, name, values, timeout)
```

Two normalizations belong to the adapter boundary and nowhere else:
- **Names**: the service layer always speaks FQDN (`_acme-challenge.example.com`). Route53 takes FQDN; GoDaddy takes the relative label (`_acme-challenge`), or `@` for the apex. The adapter converts.
- **TXT quoting**: Route53 requires each TXT string wrapped in double quotes and chunked at 255 chars; GoDaddy stores raw. The adapter quotes/strips. Getting this wrong silently breaks both SES verification and ACME, so it gets its own test.

**Credentials are forced for GoDaddy** and checked in `services/dns.get_adapter()`, not at the call sites: a `provider="godaddy"` Domain whose `credential` is null, inactive, or `verified=False` raises `me.ValueException("No working DNS credential for this domain", code=400)` before any network call. Route53 uses the process AWS credentials (`settings.AWS_KEY`/`AWS_SECRET`/`AWS_REGION`), same as every other `mojo/helpers/aws/*` helper.

**Purchase is Route53-only.** `services/registrar.py` refuses a purchase or a hosted-zone create for any `provider="godaddy"` domain with an explicit "GoDaddy domains are management-only" error, not a generic 403.

**Permission vocabulary**: fine-grained `view_dns` / `manage_dns`, with **`security`** as the domain-category umbrella (per `.claude/rules/models.md`, every RestMeta carries the category alongside the fine-grained perms). `security` is the right category: DNS authority and private-key custody are security-boundary operations, and a `security` holder is already an org admin. **`DOMAIN_CATEGORIES` in `mojo/helpers/perms.py` is NOT widened** — memory.md is explicit that adding categories casually is a bug pattern; `view_dns`/`manage_dns` are ordinary fine-grained perms that do not expand.

- `VIEW_PERMS = ["view_dns", "manage_dns", "security"]`
- `SAVE_PERMS = ["manage_dns", "security"]`
- `DELETE_PERMS = ["manage_dns", "security"]`

Every model that carries a `group` FK gets native group scoping for free (`mojo/models/rest.py:233` keys on `hasattr(cls, "group")`); `Certificate` has no direct group and declares `GROUP_FIELD = "domain__group"`.

**Settings** (all read via `settings.get(NAME, default)` at call time — no new defaults module; documented in `docs/django_developer/helpers/` settings reference and the dnsman docs):

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `DNSMAN_PURCHASE_ENABLED` | `False` | Global kill switch for any real-money call |
| `DNSMAN_MAX_DOMAIN_PRICE` | `50.00` | Refuse quotes above this (premium domains) |
| `DNSMAN_QUOTE_TTL_MINUTES` | `15` | Quote/confirm-token lifetime |
| `DNSMAN_REGISTRANT_CONTACT` | `{}` | ICANN contact dict; purchase refuses when incomplete |
| `DNSMAN_ALLOWED_RECORD_TYPES` | `["A","AAAA","CNAME","TXT","MX","SRV","CAA","NS"]` | Apex NS/SOA still refused (see below) |
| `DNSMAN_ACME_DIRECTORY_URL` | Let's Encrypt **staging** | Defaults to staging so an unconfigured deploy can never burn prod rate limits |
| `DNSMAN_ACME_CONTACT_EMAIL` | `None` | ACME account contact |
| `DNSMAN_CERT_RENEW_DAYS` | `30` | Renew when fewer days remain |
| `DNSMAN_CERT_SYNC_CHANNEL` | `"certs"` | Jobs channel the cert-updated broadcast goes to |
| `DNSMAN_DNS_PROPAGATION_TIMEOUT` | `300` | Seconds to wait for a TXT to be visible authoritatively |

### Implementation steps

#### Stage 0 — Baseline (before any edit)

Per `.claude/rules/build-baseline.md`: run `bin/run_tests --agent`, read `var/test_failures.json`, record total/passed/failed/skipped plus the names of any pre-existing failures as a `## Notes` comment on the board item. Red baseline → stop and tell the user before writing code.

#### Stage 1 — `mojo/helpers/aws/route53.py` (model-free primitives)

Follows the `mojo/helpers/aws/*` house style: module-level functions, explicit `access_key`/`secret_key`/`region` args falling back to settings, `objict` returns, no Django imports, **no type hints**. Two clients: `_domains_client()` is hardcoded to `us-east-1` (the Route53 Domains endpoint is us-east-1 only); `_dns_client()` uses the configured region.

- `check_availability(name, ...)` → `objict(name, status, available, price, currency, tld, tld_supported, privacy_supported)`. `status` is the **raw AWS enum**; `available` is **tri-state**: `True` for `AVAILABLE*`, `False` for `UNAVAILABLE*`/`RESERVED`, **`None` for `PENDING`/`DONT_KNOW`** ("the registry did not answer — retry"). `INVALID_NAME_FOR_TLD` raises a clean validation error. A `list_prices` miss sets `tld_supported=False` and never raises.
- `list_prices(tld)` → registration/renewal price for the TLD.
- `supports_privacy(tld)` → `tld not in TLDS_WITHOUT_PRIVACY`, a curated module constant (`us`, `ca`, `eu`, `in`, `sg`, `com.au`, `co.nz`, … with a comment pointing at the AWS TLD table). AWS exposes no API for this, so it is a maintained list and is documented as best-effort; the register call additionally tolerates AWS rejecting privacy for an unlisted TLD (see edge cases).
- `register(name, contact, years=1, auto_renew=True, privacy=True)` → `register_domain` with the same contact for Admin/Registrant/Tech and all three `PrivacyProtect*` flags; returns the OperationId.
- `operation_detail(op_id)`; `list_operations(submitted_since)` — the crash-window reconciliation probe.
- `get_domain_detail(name)` → contacts, expiry, nameservers, privacy flags, auto-renew.
- `update_contacts(name, contact)` → `update_domain_contact`; `update_privacy(name, enabled)` → `update_domain_contact_privacy`; `update_auto_renew(name, enabled)` → `enable_domain_auto_renew`/`disable_domain_auto_renew`.
- `find_zone_id(name)` → `list_hosted_zones_by_name`, **exact** name match (the API returns a lexical page, so a prefix match would silently pick a neighbouring zone).
- `create_hosted_zone(name)` — needed for adopt-with-no-zone and for a purchased domain whose auto-created zone is missing.
- `list_records(zone_id)` — follows `IsTruncated`/`NextRecordName`+`NextRecordType`.
- `upsert_record(zone_id, rtype, name, values, ttl)` / `delete_record(zone_id, rtype, name, values)` → `change_resource_record_sets`, **refusing apex `NS`/`SOA` and any name not suffixed by the zone's domain**. Returns the ChangeId.
- `get_change(change_id)` → `INSYNC`/`PENDING`, used as the first propagation gate.

All list/paginate helpers verified present in the installed SDK (`boto3 1.42.73`, checked in this repo's venv during scoping).

*Commit 1: route53 helper + its unit tests.*

#### Stage 2 — App skeleton + models

`mojo/apps/dnsman/apps.py` (`DnsmanConfig`, `name = "mojo.apps.dnsman"`, `verbose_name = "DNS Manager"`), package `__init__` files, and the INSTALLED_APPS entry in `bin/create_testproject`.

Five models, one per file, all `created`/`modified` per `.claude/rules/models.md`:

1. **`models/dns_credential.py` — `DnsCredential(MojoSecrets, MojoModel)`**
   `group` FK (`account.Group`, null — a null group is a house/platform credential), `name`, `provider` (default `"godaddy"`), `is_active` (default True), `verified` (default False), `verified_at`, `domain_count` (how many domains the account held at verification — a health signal, never the list), `last_error` (null). Secrets: `api_key`, `api_secret`. Properties `api_key_masked` (last 4) and `api_secret_masked`; **no property ever returns a raw secret in a graph**. Graphs list explicit fields only; `default` includes `api_key_masked`/`api_secret_masked` and nothing else secret-adjacent. `NO_SAVE_FIELDS` blocks `verified`, `verified_at`, `domain_count`, `provider`, `group`. Rotation = POST new key/secret to the link endpoint for the existing row, which re-verifies before persisting.

2. **`models/domain.py` — `Domain(models.Model, MojoModel)`**
   `group` FK (null), `user` FK (`account.User`, null, SET_NULL — who created it), `name` (unique, db_index, normalized lowercase/IDNA/no trailing dot), `provider` (`route53|godaddy`), `credential` FK → `DnsCredential` (null, SET_NULL), `status` (`pending|registering|active|failed`), `hosted_zone_id` (null), `auto_renew` (default True), `privacy` (default True), `verified` (default False — GoDaddy ownership probe result; always True for a route53 domain we registered or adopted), `registered_on`/`expires` (null), `last_error` (null), `metadata` JSONField.
   RestMeta: `CAN_CREATE = False` (rows are created only by the register/adopt/purchase services — the framework defaults `CAN_CREATE` to True and would otherwise leave a bare POST-create live on the collection route), `CAN_DELETE = True` but delete only removes our record and is documented as such (it never unregisters anything); `NO_SAVE_FIELDS = ["id", "pk", "created", "name", "provider", "status", "hosted_zone_id", "registered_on", "expires", "verified", "group", "user"]` — a declared list REPLACES the framework default, so id/pk/created must be re-included. REST save can therefore only touch `auto_renew`, `privacy`, `credential`, `metadata`; `on_rest_saved` pushes `auto_renew`/`privacy` changes to Route53 for route53-backed domains (best-effort, errors recorded in `last_error`, never a 500).
   **Invariant (ported from #391): no `failed` Domain rows persist.** Every failure path deletes the row; `DomainPurchase` is the audit trail. This keeps the unique `name` constraint guarding only live registrations.

3. **`models/domain_purchase.py` — `DomainPurchase(models.Model, MojoModel)`**
   `group` FK (null), `user` FK (null), `domain_name`, `kind` (`register`; `renew` reserved), `status` (`quoted|submitted|completed|failed|expired`), `price` Decimal(9,2) (what the registry quoted), `cost` Decimal(9,2) (our core cost — same as price today; separate column so margin/attribution can diverge without a migration), `currency` (default `USD`), `years` (default 1), `confirm_token` stored **SHA-256 hashed** (the raw token appears exactly once, in the quote response), `quote_expires`, `operation_id` (null), `error` (null), `metadata`.
   RestMeta: **read-only** — GET routes only (no SAVE route registered), `VIEW_PERMS` as above, explicit-field graphs that **exclude `confirm_token`**, which is also listed in `NO_SHOW_FIELDS` belt-and-braces.

4. **`models/acme_account.py` — `AcmeAccount(KSMSecrets, MojoModel)`**
   `directory_url` (unique), `contact_email`, `account_url` (the CA's kid), `status`, `last_error`. Secrets: `private_key_pem` (the ACME account key, P-256). One row per directory URL; created lazily on first issuance. Not exposed via REST at all (no `rest/` handler) — it is pure internal state, and that is the cheapest way to guarantee the account key never leaks.

5. **`models/certificate.py` — `Certificate(KSMSecrets, MojoModel)`**
   `domain` FK → `Domain` (CASCADE), `common_name`, `sans` JSONField (list), `status` (`pending|issuing|active|failed|revoked`), `issuer`, `serial`, `not_before`/`not_after` (null, `not_after` db_index for the renewal scan), `renew_after` (null, db_index), `cert_pem` / `chain_pem` TextFields (public material — safe to serve to an authorized caller), `acme_order_url`, `last_error`, `attempts`. Secrets (KMS envelope): `private_key_pem`.
   RestMeta: `GROUP_FIELD = "domain__group"`, `CAN_CREATE = False`, `CAN_DELETE = False` (revoke, don't delete). Graphs list explicit fields and **never** include `mojo_secrets`, `private_key_pem`, `cert_pem` or `chain_pem` — material comes only from the dedicated fetch endpoint (stage 6), so a routine list call can't spray PEMs into logs.

Then `bin/create_testproject` to generate migrations (never hand-written), and `bin/run_tests --agent` to confirm the tree is still green with the new app installed.

*Commit 2: app skeleton + models + migrations.*

#### Stage 3 — Provider dispatch + BYO onboarding

**`mojo/helpers/dns/godaddy.py`** gets one additive change: an optional `raise_on_error=False` constructor flag. When True, each method calls `resp.raise_for_status()` before parsing. Existing callers (maestro's `email_setup.py`, `aws/setup_dns.py`) keep today's swallow-everything behavior; dnsman constructs with `raise_on_error=True` so a revoked key surfaces as an error instead of a silently-False `is_domain_active`. Nothing else in that file changes.

**`services/providers/base.py`** — the four-method interface plus shared name/TXT normalization helpers.
**`services/providers/route53_provider.py`** — wraps stage 1; `wait_for_propagation` gates on `get_change` → `INSYNC`, then the authoritative probe below.
**`services/providers/godaddy_provider.py`** — wraps `DNSManager`. Two GoDaddy semantics to encode explicitly: `edit_record` is a PUT that **replaces every record of that (type, name) pair**, so `upsert_record` must send the full desired value list; and `delete_record` has no direct API — deleting means PUTting the remaining values, or (when none remain) using the type-level replace with an empty array, which GoDaddy rejects for some types. Where a true delete is impossible the adapter raises a clear "GoDaddy cannot delete the last record of this type" error rather than silently no-opping. `wait_for_propagation` has only the authoritative probe (no ChangeInfo equivalent).

**`mojo/helpers/dns/probe.py`** (new) — `wait_for_txt(fqdn, expected_values, timeout, interval=5)`: resolves the zone's authoritative NS via dnspython and queries **those servers directly**, so a cached recursive answer can't produce a false negative (or a false positive on a stale value). Returns `(ok, seen_values)`. dnspython is already a hard dependency.

**`services/dns.py`** — the single dispatch surface:
- `get_adapter(domain)` — the fail-closed credential gate described in Architecture.
- `list_records(user, domain)` / `upsert_record(...)` / `delete_record(...)` — resolve the Domain, gate permissions (`view_dns` for read, `manage_dns` for write, group-scoped), require `status="active"`, enforce `DNSMAN_ALLOWED_RECORD_TYPES`, refuse apex `NS`/`SOA` and out-of-zone names, then delegate.

**`services/onboarding.py`**:
- `link_credential(group, provider, api_key, api_secret, name=None, credential=None)` — constructs a `DNSManager(raise_on_error=True)`, calls `get_domains()` purely to prove the key works, stores **only the count**, sets `verified=True`/`verified_at`, and persists the secrets. Failure → `verified=False`, `last_error`, and a 400 with the provider's message; secrets are still stored only if the caller is rotating an already-verified credential (a failed first link persists nothing). Passing `credential=` rotates in place.
- `register_existing(group, user, name, credential)` — the self-serve BYO path: `get_domain_info(name)` through the credential; the account must actually hold the domain and it must be ACTIVE. On success creates `Domain(provider="godaddy", status="active", verified=True, credential=…)`. On failure, nothing is created. **No endpoint ever returns the credential's domain list** — the probe is per-name, so a member can only confirm a domain they already named.
- `adopt_route53(group, user, name)` — `find_zone_id(name)`; if absent and `create_zone=True`, `create_hosted_zone`. Creates `Domain(provider="route53", status="active", verified=True, hosted_zone_id=…)` with no purchase and no money. **Requires `manage_dns` AND `request.user.is_superuser`** — adopting hands a group control of a zone in the house AWS account, which for any non-superuser would be a cross-tenant zone-claim primitive (#391 decision 9, carried over verbatim).

*Commit 3: dispatch + BYO onboarding + record CRUD, with tests.*

#### Stage 4 — Purchase, WHOIS, privacy

**`services/registrar.py`** — the money path, with #391's hardened semantics ported in full:

- `search(user, name)` — validate/normalize the name, `check_availability`, attach `privacy_supported`. Read-only, no row created, `view_dns`. A tri-state `None` answer returns `available: null` with a "retry" reason.
- `quote(group, user, name, years=1)` — checks, in this order: `DNSMAN_PURCHASE_ENABLED`; caller holds `manage_dns` on the group; `DNSMAN_REGISTRANT_CONTACT` complete; name/TLD valid and supported; no existing `Domain` row for the name (all rows are live by invariant); availability is definitively `True` (an indeterminate answer creates **no** row); price ≤ `DNSMAN_MAX_DOMAIN_PRICE`. Creates `DomainPurchase(status="quoted")` with a hashed 48-char token and `quote_expires`; returns purchase id, price, currency, raw token, expiry, `privacy_supported`.
- `purchase(group, user, purchase_id, token)` — the one irreversible mutation:
  1. `transaction.atomic()` + `select_for_update()` on the purchase row. Verify token hash, TTL, and **`status == "quoted"` as a compare-and-swap under the lock** (a concurrent second call sees a non-`quoted` status and gets the uniform 400). Re-check the kill switch and the caller's permission. **Create `Domain(status="registering")` inside the transaction**, so the unique-name collision fires *before* any money moves. Set the purchase `submitted`. Commit.
  2. Only after commit: `route53.register(...)`; store `operation_id` on the purchase row.
  3. `register` raising → purchase `failed` + `error`, Domain row deleted.
  A crash between commit and the AWS call leaves `submitted` with **no `operation_id`** — a state the poller reconciles. There is no window in which money may have moved with nothing durable recorded, and **no single-call purchase path exists anywhere**.
- `poll_pending()` — idempotent, three duties:
  - `submitted` **with** `operation_id`: `operation_detail`; `SUCCESSFUL` → (status-guarded so a double observation can't double-flip) purchase `completed`, Domain `active` + `hosted_zone_id` from `find_zone_id` + `registered_on`/`expires` from `get_domain_detail`; `ERROR`/`FAILED` → purchase `failed` + error, **Domain row deleted**.
  - `submitted` **without** `operation_id` (the crash window): `list_operations(submitted_since=purchase.created)` probed for a `REGISTER_DOMAIN` operation matching the name; found → adopt its id and continue normally; nothing after 30 minutes → purchase `failed` ("registration never reached AWS"), Domain deleted, `logit.error` for ops.
  - Expire stale `quoted` rows past their TTL.
- `get_contacts(user, domain)` / `update_contacts(user, domain, contact)` / `set_privacy(user, domain, enabled)` — WHOIS surface, `manage_dns` for writes, route53-only (a GoDaddy domain returns the management-only error). `set_privacy` refuses up front for a TLD in `TLDS_WITHOUT_PRIVACY` with an explicit, user-actionable message.

**`cronjobs.py`** — `@schedule(minutes="*/5")` → `registrar.poll_pending()`. The **string** cron-field form is mandatory: `minutes=5` TypeErrors inside the matcher and the job silently never runs (`mojo/helpers/cron.py`; `mojo/apps/shortlink/cronjobs.py` is the working precedent).

**REST handlers** (thin, one concern per file, all `request.DATA`, dynamic segments at the end only):
- `rest/domain.py` — `@md.URL('domain')` + `@md.URL('domain/<int:pk>')` + `@md.uses_model_security(Domain)` → `Domain.on_rest_request`.
- `rest/credential.py` — same shape for `DnsCredential`, plus `@md.POST('credential/link')` → `onboarding.link_credential`.
- `rest/purchase.py` — `@md.GET('purchase')` / `@md.GET('purchase/<int:pk>')` → `DomainPurchase.on_rest_request`; `@md.POST('registrar/search')`, `@md.POST('registrar/quote')`, `@md.POST('registrar/purchase')`, `@md.POST('registrar/adopt')`, `@md.POST('registrar/register-existing')`.
- `rest/dns.py` — `@md.GET('dns')` (param `domain=<pk>`), `@md.POST('dns')` (upsert), `@md.POST('dns/delete')`.
- `rest/whois.py` — `@md.GET('whois')` (param `domain=<pk>`), `@md.POST('whois')` (update contacts), `@md.POST('whois/privacy')`.

Every non-RestMeta handler calls `Domain.rest_check_permission_or_raise(request, "VIEW_PERMS"/"SAVE_PERMS", instance)` explicitly — `uses_model_security` does not gate custom pk-fetching endpoints (a lesson already recorded in project memory).

*Commit 4: purchase + WHOIS + REST + cron, with tests.*

#### Stage 5 — Email integration

- **`mojo/helpers/aws/ses_domain.py`**: add `apply_dns_records_route53(domain, records, zone_id=None, access_key=None, secret_key=None)` — the twin of `apply_dns_records_godaddy` at line ~1074. Resolves the zone when not given, upserts each record through `mojo/helpers/aws/route53.py`, quoting TXT values. Existing signatures untouched.
- **`mojo/apps/dnsman/services/email.py`**: `apply_records(domain_obj, records)` — provider dispatch over the same `DnsRecord` list, so a caller never picks a provider; and `onboard_email_domain(email_domain)` — the one-call path: find the dnsman `Domain` by name (404 with a clear message when the domain isn't held here), run `ses_domain.onboard_domain(dns_mode="manual")` to compute records, apply them through the dispatch, then return the SES result plus what was applied. This is what makes `EmailDomain.dns_mode="route53"` real for the first time.
- **`mojo/apps/aws/models/email_domain.py`**: fix the graph leak — `default.extra` currently exposes **`aws_key` unmasked** (line ~144). Replace with `aws_key_masked` (a new property mirroring `aws_secret_masked`); the raw `aws_key` property stays for internal callers but leaves every graph.
- **`mojo/apps/aws/rest/email_ops.py`**: `@md.URL("email/domain/<int:pk>/onboard")` gains an optional `use_dnsman` flag that routes through `dnsman.services.email.onboard_email_domain` instead of the ad-hoc `godaddy_key`/`godaddy_secret` request parameters — the credential comes from the linked `DnsCredential`, so API secrets stop travelling in request bodies. The old parameters keep working (deprecated in docs) so nothing downstream breaks in this release.
- **Email-setup audit** written up as `docs/django_developer/dnsman/EmailSetupAudit.md`: what `email_ops`/`ses_domain`/`EmailDomain` do today, the `dns_mode="route53"` stub that was never implemented, the credentials-in-request-body pattern, the fixed `aws_key` graph leak, and what dnsman now supersedes.

*Commit 5: email integration + graph-leak fix + audit doc.*

#### Stage 6 — Certificates

**`mojo/helpers/acme/`** — a minimal, DNS-01-only ACMEv2 client built on libraries already installed (`cryptography` for keys/CSR/PEM, `requests` for transport, `jwt.utils` for `base64url_encode` and `der_to_raw_signature`). No new dependency.

- `jws.py` — `sign(payload, key, protected_header)` assembles the **flattened JSON** JWS by hand: base64url the protected header and payload, sign `protected + "." + payload` with ES256, convert the DER signature to raw R‖S. Assembled manually rather than via `PyJWS.encode` deliberately: PyJWT injects `typ` into the header, and RFC 8555 servers are strict about the protected header's contents. Also `thumbprint(key)` (RFC 7638 JWK SHA-256) for the key authorization.
- `client.py` — `AcmeClient(directory_url, account_key)`: `directory()`, `new_nonce()`, `_post(url, payload)` with **`badNonce` retry** and `Retry-After` honoring, `new_account(contact)` → account URL (kid), `new_order(identifiers)`, `get_authorization(url)`, `dns01_challenge(authz)` → `(challenge_url, token)`, `key_authorization_digest(token)` → the base64url SHA-256 TXT value, `answer_challenge(url)`, `poll_order(url)`, `finalize(order, csr_der)`, `download_certificate(url)` → the full PEM chain. `make_csr(key, names)` builds the CSR with a SAN extension covering every name.
- Errors map ACME problem documents to a `me.ValueException` carrying the CA's `detail`, so a rate-limit or a failed validation is legible in the purchase/cert row rather than a bare 500.

**`mojo/apps/dnsman/services/certs.py`**:
- `_get_account()` — loads or lazily creates the `AcmeAccount` for `DNSMAN_ACME_DIRECTORY_URL` (generating a P-256 key into KMS-backed secrets and registering it with the CA).
- `request_certificate(user, domain, names=None)` — `manage_dns`; defaults `names` to `[domain.name, "*." + domain.name]`; creates `Certificate(status="pending")` and publishes an async job. Refuses if an `active` cert already covers exactly those names and isn't inside its renewal window.
- `issue(certificate)` — the whole DNS-01 dance, and the only place the two providers matter: new order → for each authorization, compute the TXT value and **upsert `_acme-challenge.<name>` through the provider dispatch** (a wildcard and its base name share one TXT record name and need **both values present simultaneously** — the adapter's value-list API is what makes that possible, and it is exactly the case that breaks naive implementations) → `wait_for_propagation` (Route53: `get_change` INSYNC, then the authoritative probe; GoDaddy: authoritative probe only, since there is no ChangeInfo API) → answer each challenge → poll → finalize with a fresh P-256 CSR → download the chain → store `cert_pem`/`chain_pem` and the private key into KMS secrets, set `not_before`/`not_after`/`serial`/`issuer` and `renew_after = not_after - DNSMAN_CERT_RENEW_DAYS` → **always** clean up the `_acme-challenge` records, success or failure → publish the sync broadcast. Failure sets `status="failed"` + `last_error` + increments `attempts`; the challenge cleanup runs in a `finally`.
- `renew_due()` — `Certificate.objects.filter(status="active", renew_after__lte=now)` → one job each.
- `revoke(user, certificate)` — ACME `revokeCert`, status → `revoked`.

**`asyncjobs.py`** — `issue_certificate(payload)` and `renew_certificate(payload)` handlers (issuance takes minutes; it must not run in a request). **`cronjobs.py`** — `@schedule(minutes="0", hours="*/6")` → publish a renewal job per due certificate.

**Sync surface** (consumers pull; dnsman never pushes into a box):
- On every successful issue/renew, `jobs.publish(func="…", channel=settings.get("DNSMAN_CERT_SYNC_CHANNEL", "certs"), payload={"certificate": pk, "domain": name, "not_after": …}, broadcast=True)` — every runner subscribed to that channel is told a cert changed. The payload carries **no material**.
- `@md.GET('certificate/<int:pk>/material')` — returns `cert_pem`, `chain_pem`, `private_key_pem`. Explicitly gated with `Certificate.rest_check_permission_or_raise(request, "SAVE_PERMS", cert)` (i.e. `manage_dns`, not view), logs an access line via `logit`, and is the **only** path by which a private key ever leaves the database. Documented as the endpoint a serving box's sync job calls with its own API key.

*Commit 6: ACME client + certificate service + cron/jobs + sync surface, with tests.*

#### Stage 7 — Permissions sweep, docs, CHANGELOG

Re-read every handler against `.claude/rules/rest.md` and `core.md`: `request.DATA` only, no type hints in new framework code, `logit` not `logging`, explicit permission checks on every custom endpoint, zero secrets in any graph (grep the graphs for `api_key`, `api_secret`, `private_key`, `mojo_secrets`). Then docs + CHANGELOG (below), then the post-build agent trio.

*Commit 7: docs + CHANGELOG.*

### Edge cases and error handling

- **Indeterminate availability** (`PENDING`/`DONT_KNOW` — real registry behavior on some TLDs): `available: null`, "retry later", no purchase row.
- **`INVALID_NAME_FOR_TLD`** → 400 validation error. **`UNAVAILABLE_PREMIUM`** → unavailable with a reason (we do not do premium pricing).
- **Unsupported TLD** (`list_prices` miss) → `tld_supported: false`, clean refusal, never an exception.
- **Concurrent purchase of the same quote** → the CAS-under-lock admits exactly one; the loser gets a uniform 400 with no detail about which check failed.
- **Crash after commit, before/during `register_domain`** → `submitted` with no `operation_id`; the poller adopts the real operation from `list_operations` or fails the row after 30 minutes with an ops log line. Never a silent untracked registration.
- **Privacy refused by AWS for an unlisted TLD** → the register call catches the specific privacy-related `InvalidInput`, retries **once** with privacy off, and records `privacy=False` + a `metadata` note. A registration must not fail purely because our curated TLD list is stale, but the row must never claim privacy it does not have.
- **GoDaddy credential revoked mid-life** → the next dispatch call raises through `raise_on_error=True`; the service marks `verified=False` + `last_error` and returns an actionable 400. All DNS ops for that account fail closed until it is re-linked.
- **GoDaddy delete of the last record of a type** → explicit "not supported by the provider" error, never a silent no-op.
- **TXT quoting/chunking**: Route53 values are quoted and split at 255 chars; GoDaddy values are raw. Covered by a dedicated adapter test in both directions.
- **Wildcard + apex sharing `_acme-challenge`** → both digests in one record set, written in a single upsert; the cleanup removes the whole set.
- **Propagation timeout** → issuance fails cleanly with `last_error` naming the record and the values actually seen; challenge records are still cleaned up.
- **ACME rate limits / `badNonce`** → `badNonce` retries automatically; rate-limit problem documents surface the CA's `detail` verbatim into `last_error`. The staging directory is the default precisely so an unconfigured deploy cannot consume prod limits.
- **KMS unavailable** → `KSMSecrets.secrets` swallows decrypt failures and returns empty; the cert material endpoint must therefore treat an empty `private_key_pem` as a 503 ("cert material temporarily unavailable"), not as "no key".
- **Domain deleted while a cert exists** → FK CASCADE removes the certs; the sync broadcast is not re-published, and the doc tells consumers to treat a 404 on material fetch as "stop serving this cert".
- **Name normalization** everywhere: lowercase, strip trailing dot, IDNA-encode before any provider call; reject names containing spaces, paths, or underscores at the edge.

### Testing plan

`tests/test_dnsman/`, run with `bin/run_tests --agent -t test_dnsman`. Every test uses `from testit import helpers as th` + `@th.django_unit_test()`, imports the module under test inside the function, gives every assert a descriptive message, and deletes its own rows before creating them (long-lived DB rule).

**The server-isolation split matters here**: `opts.client` reaches a *separate* server process, so `mock.patch` never affects it. Therefore all AWS/GoDaddy/ACME-touching logic is tested **in-process against the services**, and the REST tests exercise only what needs no network — permissions, validation, scoping, and the disabled-purchase path.

1. `1_route53_helper.py` — in-process, boto3 clients patched at the module's `_domains_client`/`_dns_client` factories: availability tri-state (available / unavailable / `PENDING`→None / `INVALID_NAME_FOR_TLD`→error), unsupported TLD, `find_zone_id` exact-match (a lexically adjacent zone must NOT match), `list_records` pagination across `IsTruncated`, apex NS/SOA refusal, out-of-zone name refusal.
2. `2_providers.py` — adapter parity: the same logical upsert against a mocked Route53 and a mocked `DNSManager` produces the right provider-specific calls; FQDN↔relative conversion including the apex `@`; TXT quoting/chunking both ways; multi-value TXT; GoDaddy last-record delete raises.
3. `3_credentials.py` — link verifies and stores; a failed first link persists nothing; rotation re-verifies; `register_existing` succeeds only when the account holds an ACTIVE domain; **no endpoint or service return value ever contains the account's domain list**; a `provider="godaddy"` Domain with a missing/inactive/unverified credential fails closed before any network call.
4. `4_registrar.py` — quote happy path; kill-switch off → refusal without touching AWS; incomplete registrant contact → refusal; price cap; duplicate name; indeterminate availability → no row; token single-use + TTL expiry; purchase happy path → Domain `registering`; **second purchase on the same quote → uniform 400 (CAS)**; boto error → purchase `failed` and **no orphan Domain**; `poll_pending` completes / fails / is idempotent under double observation; **submitted-without-operation_id reconciliation** (adopts from `list_operations`; times out to failed + Domain deleted); privacy refused → single retry without privacy, `privacy=False` recorded.
5. `5_certs.py` — the ACME client against a fully mocked CA (`requests` patched): JWS protected-header shape (`alg`/`nonce`/`url`/`jwk`-or-`kid` and nothing else), thumbprint/key-authorization digest against the RFC 8555 example vector, `badNonce` retry, order→authz→challenge→finalize→download happy path, problem-document mapping. Then the service: wildcard + apex produce **one** TXT record set with **two** values; challenge records are cleaned up on success **and** on failure; a propagation timeout fails cleanly; `renew_due` selects only certs past `renew_after`; the sync broadcast fires with no material in the payload.
6. `6_rest_permissions.py` — REST against the live dev server with `DNSMAN_PURCHASE_ENABLED` default False (set via `th.server_settings(...)`, never `override_settings`): quote/purchase return the clean disabled refusal without touching AWS; domain/credential/purchase list+detail scoping; `adopt` denied for a non-superuser; DNS endpoints refuse on a non-active domain; `requires_params` 400s; graph assertions that **no** response body anywhere contains `api_secret`, `private_key_pem`, `mojo_secrets`, or an unmasked `api_key`.
7. `7_tenant_isolation.py` — the cross-tenant matrix: a member of group A never sees or touches B's domains, credentials, purchases, or certificates; `?group=` never widens; uniform 403s.
8. `tests/test_aws/` — one added case asserting `EmailDomain`'s default graph no longer contains `aws_key` and does contain `aws_key_masked`.

Full-suite green (`bin/run_tests --agent`) against the stage-0 baseline is the close condition. One test run at a time — never parallel agents.

### Documentation plan

**django_developer track** — new `docs/django_developer/dnsman/`:
- `README.md` — what dnsman is, the model map, the provider-dispatch diagram, the permission vocabulary, every setting key, and the "which layer owns what" split (mechanism here, policy in the consumer).
- `Domains.md` — Domain lifecycle, the no-failed-rows invariant, adopt vs register-existing vs purchase, name normalization.
- `Providers.md` — the adapter interface, Route53 vs GoDaddy semantic differences (PUT-replaces, no delete of a last record, no ChangeInfo, TXT quoting), and how to add a third provider.
- `Registrar.md` — the purchase flow with its concurrency and crash-ordering guarantees, plus the **ops runbook**: enabling purchases, filling `DNSMAN_REGISTRANT_CONTACT`, the us-east-1 quirk, the **canary purchase** (Route53 Domains has no sandbox — the first real registration must be a cheap house domain), **ICANN registrant-email verification** (a new contact email must be verified within 15 days or registrations suspend — the house inbox must be monitored), and the **60-day post-registration transfer lock**.
- `Certificates.md` — the ACME DNS-01 flow, the account key, KMS custody, renewal cron, the sync-broadcast contract and the material endpoint, the staging-by-default setting, Let's Encrypt rate limits, and the documented HTTP-01-on-box fallback for zones we cannot touch.
- `EmailSetupAudit.md` — the stage-5 audit.

**web_developer track** — new `docs/web_developer/dnsman/README.md`: every endpoint with request/response shapes and the permissions needed, the search→quote→purchase contract (including that the confirm token is shown exactly once), the DNS record API, WHOIS/privacy, certificate status and material fetch, and the error shapes.

**Indexes**: add a `dnsman/` row to both root `README.md` tables. **`CHANGELOG.md`**: a new entry describing the app, the endpoints, the `EmailDomain` graph fix (a behavior change consumers can see), and that purchasing ships disabled with ACME pointed at staging.

### Design decisions

1. **One build, seven staged commits.** The requester chose a single build over phasing. The stage boundaries are chosen so each commit leaves a green tree and a coherent feature: helper → models → DNS management → purchase → email → certs → docs. If the session must stop, it stops on a commit, not mid-feature. Flagged plainly: this is a large build for one session, and the risk is fatigue, not design — the design is fully specified above precisely so a resumed session does not have to re-derive it.
2. **Framework app, not a helper-only layer.** Domains, credentials, and certs are stateful and permissioned; they need models, REST, and cron. `mojo/helpers/aws/route53.py` stays model-free so it is reusable on its own (and so `ses_domain.py` can call it without importing the app).
3. **`DnsCredential` as its own model, not fields on `Domain`.** One GoDaddy account holds many domains and rotation must happen in exactly one place. Rejected: credentials on the Domain row (N copies to rotate) and credentials in settings (kills per-tenant BYO).
4. **Uniform adapters over per-call branching.** The two providers differ in ways that will bite silently — name form, TXT quoting, replace-vs-upsert, no propagation API. Confining that to two adapter files behind one interface is what lets email and ACME each be written once. Rejected: `if domain.provider == …` at every call site.
5. **`security` as the domain category, `DOMAIN_CATEGORIES` untouched.** Adding a `dns` category would make bare `dns` expand to `view_dns`+`manage_dns` platform-wide; memory.md records that widening that set casually is a known bug pattern. `security` is the existing category whose holders should legitimately have this reach.
6. **No end-user purchase policy here.** Only a global kill switch, a price cap, a complete-contact requirement, and the quote→confirm token — mechanisms, not policy. Allowlists, monthly caps, credits, and the confirm UX belong to maestro (#391), which is exactly the split decision this item exists to honor.
7. **ACME client written in-repo** (the recommendation the requester asked for). DNS-01 is a small, well-specified subset of ACME, and every primitive it needs is already a hard dependency: `cryptography` for the account/cert keys and the CSR, `requests` for transport, `jwt.utils` for base64url and DER→raw signature conversion. Verified during scoping that ES256 signing and those utilities are present in this venv. The alternative — certbot's `acme` package — is more battle-tested but adds `josepy` + `pyOpenSSL` to a **published** framework that most consumers will never use for certificates, forcing an optional-extra with lazy imports and a dev-group install just to test it. Roughly 250–300 lines of protocol code, fully mockable, is the better trade here. If issuance proves flaky in practice, swapping the client behind `services/certs.py` is a contained change.
8. **Let's Encrypt staging is the default directory.** An unconfigured deploy that starts issuing must not burn production rate limits. Going live is a deliberate settings change, documented in the runbook.
9. **Certificate material leaves only through one gated endpoint.** Not in any graph, not in the sync broadcast payload, `manage_dns`-gated, access-logged. The broadcast says "something changed"; the consumer authenticates and pulls.
10. **`AcmeAccount` has no REST surface at all.** The cheapest possible guarantee that the account key never appears in a response.
11. **`adopt` stays superuser-only** (#391 decision 9). It grants a group control over a hosted zone in the house AWS account; open to any `manage_dns` holder it would be a cross-tenant zone-claim primitive.
12. **`raise_on_error` added to `DNSManager` rather than changing its defaults.** maestro consumes that helper today with error-swallowing behavior; flipping it would be a silent downstream break. dnsman opts in.
